policy: Metadata/abstract verification is not a theorem audit, proof import, novelty verdict or exhaustive latest-literature search. Exact lower-bound comparisons require a separate setting contract and source theorem anchor.

sources.title: Efficient Quantum Circuits for Accurate State Preparation of Smooth, Differentiable Functions
sources.anchor: Abstract: explicit function to MPS to circuit; requested v1 HTML was unavailable in this audit
sources.scope: Prior art for function-to-MPS preparation. The ASPBE Hermite specialization must not be credited with inventing polynomial-to-MPS or sequential MPS preparation.

sources.title: Optimal (controlled) quantum state preparation and improved unitary synthesis by quantum circuits with any number of ancillary qubits
sources.anchor: Abstract and publication version notice: published arXiv v2; later v3 exists
sources.scope: Baseline for arbitrary and controlled state preparation and ancilla/depth trade-offs. Pin a version and gate model before comparing bounds.

sources.title: Circuit complexity of quantum access models for encoding classical data
sources.anchor: Results: circuit complexity lower bound; construction of LCU-based block-encoding; Methods: state preparation
sources.scope: Explicit access construction is not a free oracle. PREPARE together with SELECT and uncomputation can supply a block encoding; a single prepared state alone does not determine an arbitrary operator.

sources.title: Quantum State Preparation without Coherent Arithmetic
sources.authors: Sam McArdle; András Gilyén; Mario Berta
sources.anchor: Abstract; Physical Review Letters 136, 240603, published 18 June 2026
sources.scope: QET-based function preparation with few ancillas. Approximation, normalization and success probability remain separate costs.

sources.title: Quantum state preparation via piecewise QSVT
sources.scope: Piecewise function preparation baseline; partition access, degree, success amplification and primitive compilation must be specified before a resource comparison.

sources.title: Quantum state preparation for multivariate functions
sources.scope: Multivariate preparation baseline; a tensor-product coefficient count is not automatically polynomial in dimension.

sources.title: QKAN: quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with applications in machine learning and multivariate state preparation
sources.authors: Petr Ivashkov; Po-Wei Huang; Kelvin Koor; Lirandë Pira; Patrick Rebentrost
sources.anchor: Abstract, Introduction and Discussion: shallow compositional state preparation
sources.scope: Composition-dependent bounds, not an efficient preparation theorem for every continuous multivariate function.

sources.title: Quantum Rejection Sampling
sources.authors: Maris Ozols; Martin Roetteler; Jérémie Roland
sources.anchor: Authors' publication page: quantum state generation, query characterization and matching lower bound
sources.scope: Prior art for coherent amplitude reweighting. Novelty must be in an explicit structured envelope, guarantees, implementation or model-matched bound, not in rejection sampling itself.

sources.title: Near-optimal ground state preparation
sources.anchor: Abstract: initial overlap, spectral-gap promise, energy information and lower bounds
sources.scope: Use the promised overlap/gap model; do not erase these costs in a generic strong-correlation claim.

sources.title: Initial State Preparation for Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
sources.scope: Application motivation for trial-state construction, assessment and refinement; not a proved overlap guarantee for arbitrary molecules.

sources.title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Samplers with Kubo–Martin–Schwinger Detailed Balance Condition
sources.authors: Zhiyan Ding; Bowen Li; Lin Lin
sources.anchor: Article abstract and Gibbs-sampler construction; Communications in Mathematical Physics 406, 67
sources.scope: Invariant Gibbs state and efficient mixing are different obligations. A low-temperature polynomial mixing claim needs additional model-specific evidence.

sources.title: Efficient quantum state preparation on Quantinuum hardware (candidate reference)
sources.authors: Unverified in a primary source during this audit
sources.anchor: User-supplied arXiv identifier; primary fetch failed; do not use reported hardware numbers as evidence
sources.scope: Retained in the candidate queue rather than silently promoted from secondary indexing.

sources.title: Samplinglib theorem-publication and conceptual-mirror protocols
sources.anchor: Author once; graph contribution; independent encoder–denoiser; unchanged historical audit debt
sources.scope: Design attribution. QuantumComputinglib has its own register, oracle, clean-ancilla and resource contracts; Samplinglib is not an imported Lean dependency.

sources.title: Asymptotically Optimal Quantum Circuits for Comparators and Incrementers
sources.anchor: Sections 2–6; Figures 3–5; Eq. (16) controlled-adder rewrite; Eq. (17) quantum–quantum comparator contract
sources.scope: Primary source for the partial PromiseGateOptimization route and the planned source-faithful adder/comparator/incrementer formalization. Existing generic controlled-conjugation and dirty-flag lemmas do not certify the complete paper circuits or optimality claims.

sources.title: Representation-theoretic methods in quantum information theory
sources.anchor: Course notes: finite-dimensional QIT foundations, representation theory, Schur–Weyl duality and symmetry-based QIT applications
sources.scope: Planned curriculum anchor for a future Quantum Information part. Source registration is not a claim that its theorems have been formalized locally.

sources.title: Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation
sources.anchor: 29 April 2026 public 447-page edition; Parts I–IV from background/foundations through block encoding, QSP/QSVT, simulation, linear systems/differential equations and open systems
sources.scope: Planned curriculum anchor for quantum scientific computing. Reuse existing ASPBE state-preparation/block-encoding nodes; do not duplicate Chapter 9 under a second API. The user-supplied PDF is not vendored because this edition is publicly hosted.
